key_insight: AIDE^2 shows that an AI research agent can recursively improve its own code, turning each accepted rewrite into a better editor for the next round.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path to raising AI R&D productivity by continuously improving the agent’s search, memory, and optimization policies rather than only the target models it develops.
method: Agent proposes edits to its own codebase.
Each variant is benchmarked on AI R&D tasks and selected using hidden evaluations.
Winning edits are chained over time in an autonomous self-improvement loop.
evidence_signal: In an 8-day autonomous run, AIDE^2 produced seven successive improvements that generalized to four held-out benchmarks, including out-of-distribution weather forecasting, and reduced reward hacking from 55% to 32%.
watch_item: The gains come from a controlled evaluation loop with hidden benchmarks, so real-world robustness, safety, and compute cost may differ when the system is deployed more broadly.
paper_title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
